rules.text: Click a green box to select it. The selected box has a white center; the others have a dark center. Every click costs 1 step, even on empty floor or on the box that is already selected.

rules.text: Clicking is the only control. Click an arm to pick it: the picked arm is drawn with a white outline and the others with dark gray. At the start of a level the arm nearest the top-left corner is already picked.
Click anywhere that isn't an arm and the picked arm jumps so its center is where you clicked. Arms of any blob can be picked, one at a time.
There is no undo. RESET restarts the level, with every arm back in place, the click count back to zero and any strikes cleared.

Each blob has an outline target: a hollow ring of dots in the blob's colors. On levels 1-4 the level is won when every blob's body overlaps its own outline. Touching it is enough, the body doesn't need to be centered in it.
rules.source: r11l.py:355-367, 1758-1783, 1705-1709; engine runs on level 1: a body only touching the outline's edge still cleared the level

rules.text: A blob is a body (a small rounded square in the blob's colors with a pink dot in the middle) and two or more arms (small plus shapes with a colored center). Thin light gray lines join each arm to its body.
You never move a body directly. After every arm move the body jumps to the average position of all its arms, so moving arms drags the body around.
rules.source: r11l.py:1536-1551, 1725-1730; engine run on level 1: body went from (15,45) to (34,32) after one arm move

rules.text: Gray walls stop arms: if the arm would overlap a wall where you clicked, it doesn't move. The body is never checked against walls, so it can end up on top of one.
rules.source: r11l.py:816-830, 1553-1566, 1839-1843, 1536-1551; engine run on level 1: a click into the wall left both arms in place

rules.text: Every click costs one of the level's 60 clicks: picking an arm, moving it, and clicks into walls that do nothing. The 60th click ends the game on the spot, so you really get 59. The count starts over on each level.
rules.source: r11l.py:1406-1407, 1805-1812; arcengine/base_game.py:148-160; engine run: game over on the 60th click

rules.text: When a body lands on its outline, a white copy of the outline blinks over it a few times and then stays on while the body is there. It disappears if the body moves off. When the last one is in place, the next level loads after the blinking.
rules.source: r11l.py:411-423, 1646-1689, 1699-1709; engine runs: 23 frames on the winning move of level 1, highlight removed when the body left an outline on level 5

rules.text: The column along the left edge of the screen is the click bar. It starts white and turns black from the top down as you spend clicks.
rules.source: r11l.py:1306-1331; engine run: 31 white pixels left after 31 clicks

rules.text: Two blobs at once, each with its own color, arms and outline. Both bodies have to be on their outlines.

Light blue hazard zones (levels 2, 3 and 4). If an arm move puts any body into one, that body blinks white a few times, the arm jumps back to where it was, and you get a strike. Only bodies trigger it, not arms. The move still costs its click.
rules.source: r11l.py:86-98, 1733-1757, 1620-1644, 1786-1803; engine run on level 2: 23 frames, arm and body back in place

rules.text: Five strikes on one level ends the game. Nothing on screen counts the strikes for you.
rules.source: r11l.py:1747-1753, 1306-1331 (only the click bar is drawn); engine run on level 2: game over on the 5th hazard hit

rules.text: Some outlines belong to no blob. They look just like real ones, but the win check skips them, so they can be left empty. Level 4 has five of them, level 5 three and level 6 one.
Blobs and outlines with more than one color, split into two or three colored parts.

On levels 5 and 6 no outline has a blob of its own. An outline is filled when any body sits on it with exactly the same set of colors (white doesn't count), and the level is won when every real outline is filled.
rules.source: r11l.py:1601-1618, 1769-1783; engine runs on levels 5 and 6: with one outline filled the level did not end, and with both real outlines filled level 5 advanced and level 6 won the game

rules.text: The blobs' bodies start plain white, and food pellets appear: small blobs, part white and part one color. When a move puts a body over a pellet, the pellet's colored pixels are painted onto the body in the same spots and the pellet is gone. Only the body eats, not the arms. Level 5 has 4 pellets and level 6 has 9.
rules.source: r11l.py:464-476, 673-685, 1238-1241, 1260-1268, 1585-1599, 1731-1732; engine run on level 5: the body turned half red and the red pellet disappeared

rules.text: A later pellet can paint over a color the body already ate, so the order you eat in matters.
rules.source: r11l.py:1594-1596; engine run on level 5: blue was replaced by green, leaving red and green

trace.outcome: The later-level goal requires the right color or combination; the player's note identifies eating as the new prerequisite.
trace.revision: I need to solve a color-acquisition problem before the final placement problem.
trace.nextAction: Match each body to a feasible target color and plan a collection route that does not consume an unneeded pellet.

rules.text: Four moves only: up, down, left, right. There is no click and no undo.
The board is White pads joined by short Gray wires on black. A move slides your token along a Gray wire to the next White pad. You can only go where a wire leads.
Land on the solid Green square to clear the level. Each level has exactly one.
Your token is a Blue square with a Darker Gray dot. The dot turns to point the way you last moved.
Pressing a direction with no wire still uses one step, but nothing on the board moves -- enemies stay put too -- so you cannot use it to wait for an enemy to pass.

The step bar is a Pink line along the very bottom edge of the screen. Every arrow press uses one step, and the used part turns White. It refills on each new level: 50, 50, 35, 20, 50, 60, 30, 50 and 50 steps for levels 1 to 9.
When the bar is empty you lose. A move that spends your last step and lands you on the exit still wins.
Moves are animated one after the other: your token slides to the next pad first, then the enemies slide. You always finish your move before any enemy moves.
There are no lives. Getting killed or emptying the bar ends the attempt on the spot, and after that only RESET does anything.
RESET puts the level back the way it started: full bar, every enemy back in place.
Red square with a Purple dot: an enemy. It never moves on its own and never turns. The Purple dot is its front and shows the way it faces.
Step onto a Red enemy's pad from its side or from behind and you bite it: it is destroyed. You can never reach it head-on, because you would have to stop on the pad in front of it first.

Finish a move on the pad right in front of a Red enemy's dot and it bites: the dot turns Yellow, it lunges onto your pad and you die. It makes no difference how you got there -- walking straight at it or crossing in front of it from the side both get you killed.
Every enemy follows the same contact rule: step onto the pad an enemy is standing on and it dies; be standing on the pad an enemy moves onto and you die. Enemies do not block your moves.
The enemies take their move before the game checks for the exit. Landing on the Green square does not save you if an enemy reaches your pad on that same move.
Anything destroyed -- an enemy or your own token -- bursts into a ring of eight dots in its own color that grows once and disappears.

rules.text: Click is the only action. Clicking a blue pump or an orange gate does something. Clicking anything else, including a gray gate or a pump that can't move liquid right now, does nothing but still uses a click.
You win when every rider is level with a short stripe of its own color painted on a black wall next to its tank. The check runs after every click.

The white areas are liquid in tanks divided by black walls. The liquid settles toward one side of the screen, and that side changes by level: right on levels 1 and 5, left on 2 and 6, down on 3 and 4, up on 7. The pumps always sit on the side the liquid settles toward, and the surface is the far face of the liquid.

Blue squares are pumps. They come in pairs at the foot of a black wall, one on each side of it. Clicking one moves liquid through that wall into the tank on the pump's own side: that tank's surface moves out one step and the tank across the wall drops one step. A step is 2 pixels on levels 1-3 and 7, and 3 pixels on levels 4-6.
A pump does nothing if the tank it would drain is empty, or if the tank it would fill already reaches the end of the shorter black wall beside it.

Riders are small shapes with a darker gray cap and a colored base (yellow, green or purple), sitting on a liquid surface. You can't click them. They move only when the surface under them moves, and they go with it.

The strip along the top edge is the click budget: light pink for clicks left, darker gray for clicks used. Every click costs one. The budgets are 50, 50, 75, 50, 200, 50 and 200 for levels 1 to 7. The click that uses the last one loses, unless that same click wins the level.
RESET restarts the current level with a full budget. There is no undo; the other pump of a pair moves the liquid back, and that costs a click too.
Three tanks in a row. The middle tank has a wall on each side, so it can be filled or drained through either wall.
Three riders at once (yellow, green and purple). Each one needs a stripe of its own color, and all three have to be level at the same time.

Clicking an orange gate opens it: the gate slides back out of the way, a rider on either side slides across to the middle of the tank on the other side, and the gate slides shut. If both sides have a rider, they swap. The whole crossing plays out as one click. Clicking a gray gate does nothing.

Light gray gates set into the black walls. A gate is ready when the liquid on both sides of it is exactly level with its end nearest the liquid; it then turns orange and white brackets appear on both sides of it. When it stops being level, it goes back to light gray.

Riders are small shapes with a darker gray cap and a colored base (yellow, green or purple), sitting on a liquid surface. You can't click them. They move only when the surface under them moves, and they go with it.

The strip along the top edge is the click budget: light pink for clicks left, darker gray for clicks used. Every click costs one. The budgets are 50, 50, 75, 50, 200, 50 and 200 for levels 1 to 7. The click that uses the last one loses, unless that same click wins the level.
RESET restarts the current level with a full budget. There is no undo; the other pump of a pair moves the liquid back, and that costs a click too.
Three tanks in a row. The middle tank has a wall on each side, so it can be filled or drained through either wall.
Three riders at once (yellow, green and purple). Each one needs a stripe of its own color, and all three have to be level at the same time.

Clicking an orange gate opens it: the gate slides back out of the way, a rider on either side slides across to the middle of the tank on the other side, and the gate slides shut. If both sides have a rider, they swap. The whole crossing plays out as one click. Clicking a gray gate does nothing.

Light gray gates set into the black walls. A gate is ready when the liquid on both sides of it is exactly level with its end nearest the liquid; it then turns orange and white brackets appear on both sides of it. When it stops being level, it goes back to light gray.
Black bars in a tank's path. A tank can't be pumped past the bar, and if a rider sits on that tank, it stops early enough to leave the rider room.
